newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway C. Bank sets third fixed-term deposit rate.
newsitem.headline: Norway C. Bank sets third fixed-term deposit rate.

text.p: Norway's central bank, Norges Bank, said on Tuesday it had set an interest rate of 3.70 percent for its fixed-term deposit rate for the period July 2 to July 7.
Earlier on Tuesday the bank announced an interest rate of 3.6 percent for its fixed-term deposit rate between July 1 and July 3.
It is the third time within a week that the bank has announced a fixed interest rate.
Norges Bank regularly announces fixed-term deposits or fixed-term loans, which usually are carried out through ordinary auction, in order to control money market liquidity.

"This is clearly a signal from the central bank that there has been a normalisation of its policy regarding the crown," said one analyst. "It is saying that it wants tighter money market conditions and doesn't want to seen the crown weaken any more."

On Thursday the bank set an interest rate of 3.6 percent for its fixed-term deposit rate for the period July 1 to July 14. That time analysts said the bank appeared to be testing the market's reaction to higher money market rates to see if it was enough to stabilise the crown.
